gaps.sentence: 'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

gaps.sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

gaps.sentence: 'Could you open the window?' she asked. She asked me ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Could you...?' requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive; no could remains.

gaps.sentence: 'I don't like seafood,' he confessed. He confessed that he ___ like seafood.
gaps.explanation: Present simple negative backshifts: don't like → didn't like.

gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

gaps.sentence: 'Who broke the window?' the teacher demanded. The teacher demanded ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Demand to know + wh-clause' with statement order; past simple backshifts to past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.
